<reason>PRO kept the debate anchored to the motion's actual comparator — short-form/creator work versus traditional channel expansion — and used BBC Three and funk as plausible, non-fabricated anchors. CON was often more vivid (sovereignty, "rented shelf space," indispensability) but drifted toward a different motion: it redefined "channel" as all owned distribution including on-demand, kids' and minority-language services, then argued short-form displaces core public-service work. PRO called this smuggling, answered CON's "name the loser" question plainly (linear spin-offs and expansion launches), and exposed a tension in CON's position: CON's "nobody is launching a fifth channel, phantom fight" claim effectively concedes the motion's stated comparison, while CON's own answer to how a 19-year-old finds the broadcaster ended with "clips of that work, posted where she is." CON's best late blow — the attribution/"anonymised" floor — partly misdescribed A4.5, which explicitly said the content carries the broadcaster's name. CON's distribution-vs-prioritisation distinction was a real, live route and kept the result competitive, but PRO made the decision under the motion as written easier.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's pressure Q1 (how does a 19-year-old discover the on-demand app without meeting it in a feed?) forced CON in B4.2–B4.3 to concede clips in feeds as part of the discovery path, which PRO then crystallized in closing as CON having "walked to my side," leaving only the question of commissioning order.</best_rebuttal>
